verdicts.explanation: Table I gives σ(300 K) = 23.4 ± 0.8 mS/cm and Ea = 116 ± 12 meV for t-LLZO (1.8% vac.), this work, so the value, unit, temperature, material and computational origin all match. The 0.116 eV figure is the Table I value expressed in eV.

The Discussion says Andriyevsky et al. (ref 61) reported data only above 1350 K and that extrapolating that limit to 300 K yields ≈0.18 mS cm−1. Attributing it to literature_cited with the stated extrapolation method is correct, and Table II lists 0.18 for the Andriyevsky AIMD entry.

The paper states that Miara et al. predicted ≈0.001 mS cm−1 for t-LLZO from AIMD above 600 K, which matches the record's value, unit, temperature range and literature_cited origin. Table II also lists this as the Miara [60] entry.
